contribution.position: I hold my earlier position on reliability. I am answering qa's claim on axis:risk that error_rate is 0.4%, comfortably inside the 1% budget. That figure does not appear in artifact:perf-report, which records error_rate at 3.4% at peak load against a 1% budget. No artifact in the list contains a 0.4% measurement. If qa has a separate run, such as off-peak or a different configuration, it is not among the available artifacts, and until it is produced it cannot offset the peak-load figure. The relevant condition for the retry-storm failure mode is peak load, so a lower number measured elsewhere would not address it. I also looked at ops' point that artifact:ops-runbook documents deploy and rollback. That supports operability, but the runbook as described covers deploy and rollback only. It does not show that retry or backoff behavior is safe at an elevated error rate, which is what artifact:incident-log ties to the two sev2 incidents. The only new point since my last turn is that artifact:test-report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) is functional evidence and says nothing about behavior under load. What would change my position: a peak-load rerun with error_rate within budget, or evidence that client retry and backoff stay bounded at the measured 3.4%.
